To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
aging is associated with a loss of function in the skin microcirculation.

the skin microcirculation undergoes age-related structural and functional changes that are likely due to the loss of endothelial cell function and the accumulation of advanced glycation end-products (AGEs) in the skin.
the skin blood flow is decreased with age and the microcirculation is less able to respond to stressors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how the skin's microcirculation changes with age and the effect these changes have on skin physiology and function.
the microvasculatures of the skin, and the changes that occur with aging.
the microvascular changes that occur in the skin during normal aging and the potential clinical strategies to mitigate these changes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

aging is associated with changes in the microvascular system that are not well understood and that these changes may be responsible for some of the age-related changes in the microvasculatory reserve.
the skin microcirculation is a complex system that is influenced by multiple factors, which include the environment, the individual and the disease state.
there is a progressive decline in the microvasculatory function in aging skin.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

aging is associated with anatomic and functional changes in skin microvasculature that can be mitigated with a variety of pharmacological, nutritional, and behavioral strategies, which may improve outcomes following stress.

aging is associated with a decline in the cutaneous microcirculation that is associated with an increased risk of adverse outcomes, and that the application of a combination of pharmacologic and non-pharmacologic strategies may mitigate these effects.
aging is associated with a reduction in the number of capillaries, a reduction in the capillary density, a reduction in capillary length, and a reduction in the functional reserve of the capillaries.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the microvascular system is an important target for therapeutic interventions in aging.
the microcirculation is a key component in determining outcomes following surgical procedures, and strategies to improve microcirculatory function will improve clinical outcomes.
the skin is an ideal model for studying the effect of aging on other organs and that the microvasculatory changes in the skin may have a significant impact on the outcome of surgical procedures.
